title.narrative: Enhancing Resilience of the most marginalised and vulnerable communities affected by floods in Balasore district Odisha

description.narrative: Balasore district in Odisha is experiencing a severe flood crisis, caused by two successive spells of flooding within a span of nine days. The first spell affected 17 Gram Panchayats forcing families into temporary shelters. Before recovery could begin, a second and more destructive spell struck on June 29, 2025, following three consecutive days of intense rainfall. The deluge severely affected six blocks and one urban body. The floods have not only displaced families but also caused extensive damage to homes, agricultural land, and essential infrastructure—further compounding the hardships faced by the affected population. Damaged homes, disrupted livelihoods, and inadequate relief efforts continue to push vulnerable communities toward distress migration. This project aims to provide immediate humanitarian assistance to 500 of the most vulnerable families affected by the recent floods in Baliapal block of Balasore district, Odisha which has a significant proportion of socially and economically excluded communities Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, minorities, fishing communities, and landless laborers who are particularly vulnerable due to their limited proximity to aid, poor access to government services, and systemic marginalization. The intervention will include a combination of unconditional cash transfers and distribution of Shelter cum Non-Food Item (NFI) Kits, addressing both financial and material needs of the affected households. A total of 300 families will receive ₹4,000 each to meet urgent needs such as food, shelter, healthcare, and essential non-food items. This flexible financial support will enable families to prioritize their immediate requirements based on their specific circumstances while fostering dignity & promote early recovery.
